title: Mosaic commit conductor for cost recommendations with tiered approvals and latency sentinels
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Implement a resilient orchestrator ("mosaic commit conductor") that sequences Optimize recommendations (batching and KV-cache profiles) through a multi-stage activation pipeline. The conductor must support: 1) operator-facing tiered approval matrix, 2) traffic-canary and traffic-shadowing modes, 3) latency sentinels that automatically pause or rollback changes if P99 or tail latencies exceed configured thresholds, and 4) a simulated-traffic validation stage that runs lightweight microbenchmarks before applying to live traffic. This ticket covers the control-plane components, approval UI hooks, and the minimal runtime shims to perform staged activation and rollback. Runtime heavy-lifting (batching engine internals) will be covered in a follow-up runtime ticket.
acceptance_criteria: Conductor can accept a recommendation bundle (batching+cache profile) and create a sequenced plan with at least four stages: simulate, shadow, canary, full-rollout.
Operator UI displays a per-stage approval matrix with required approvers per customer tier and an override audit entry when manual approval is used.
Latency sentinels evaluate both request-level P99 and model-token tail latency; if either breaches configured thresholds during canary, conductor auto-pauses and creates a labeled rollback action.
A simulated-traffic step executes a deterministic microbenchmark (configured by the recommendation) and reports expected token-cost delta and latency delta before any live traffic stage.
End-to-end smoke test exists in CI that runs a simulated rollout with mocked telemetry and verifies rollback is triggered for a synthetic latency spike.
All operator actions and automated decisions are logged to the console audit stream with links to the associated PR and replay artifacts.
No changes are applied to more than 5% of production traffic without explicit two-step approval if customer tier is Enterprise.
technical_design: High-level components: 1) Conductor service (control plane) that stores staged plans, executes stage transitions, and evaluates policy plugins; 2) Policy plugins: approval-matrix plugin, latency-sentinel plugin, cost-estimation plugin; 3) Runtime shim API: light RPC to the serving orchestrator to apply/unapply configs atomically per GPU-pool; 4) Simulator harness: runs a cached KV/sequence-length subset to estimate impact; 5) Audit and observability: events emitted to Console and stored in the conductor's change log. The conductor persists state with idempotent commands and supports an optimistic lock to avoid concurrent-plan races. Stage transitions are timeboxed and require either automated pass (telemetry within thresholds) or explicit operator ack. Rollback is implemented as an inverse plan that re-applies previous known-good profiles and stamps an incident id.
rollout_plan: Stage 0 - Simulate: run simulator locally (no live traffic), produce cost/latency delta. Required: pass simulator smoke checks.
Stage 1 - Shadow: route a duplicate of 2% of requests to config in shadow mode (no client-visible effect). Collect telemetry for 24h and check sentinels.
Stage 2 - Canary: route 5% of live traffic to the new config. Latency sentinels enforced; automatic pause/rollback enabled. Requires single approver for Standard tier.
Stage 3 - Gradual roll: increase to 25% then 100% with configurable step increments. Enterprise customers require two approvers and explicit time gating.
Emergency rollback path: immediate re-apply of previous profile when sentinel breaches or operator triggers emergency revert.
Finalization: annotate rollout with telemetry summary and cost delta, close plan and create postmortem if any rollbacks occurred.
monitoring_playbook: Primary metrics: P50/P95/P99 latency (request and per-token), token-cost per 1k tokens, KV cache hit rate, queue depth, GPU util.
Sentinel rules: P99 greater than baseline * 1.3 or token-latency delta > 30% -> auto-pause and notify on-call.
Alerting: PagerDuty for on-call after a stage auto-pauses; Slack channel #optimize-rollouts for operator notifications.
Dashboards: per-canary timeline with before/after cost and latency overlays; link to replay traces and raw request samples.
Post-rollout audit: automatic snapshot of the console audit stream with the applied config and approval events.
Forwards-compatible: conductor emits structured events to allow downstream ML monitoring to compute quality regressions (not in scope for v1).
test_plan: Unit tests for conductor state machine transitions including idempotency checks.
Integration test: end-to-end simulated rollout in staging with synthetic telemetry generator that can trigger sentinels.
Chaos test: artificially delay runtime apply RPCs to validate timeouts and compensating rollback behavior.
Manual QA: operator walkthrough of approval matrix and manual override flows using a staging console build.
CI gating: PRs for conductor must include a smoke harness run that verifies no uncontrolled production API calls are made.
Load test: ensure conductor handles 200 concurrent plans in the queue without state corruption.
